{{Nihongo|'''Kunioki Mima'''|三間 圀興|Mima Kunioki|17 August 1945 – 5 January 2025}} was a Japanese [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physicist]]. He is known for his contributions to the theory of [[Turbulence|turbulent transport]] in plasmas,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hasegawa|first1=A.|last2=Mima|first2=K.|date=1978|title=Pseudo-three-dimensional turbulence in magnetized nonuniform plasma|journal=The Physics of Fluids|volume=21|issue=1|pages=87–92|doi=10.1063/1.862083|bibcode=1978PhFl...21...87H|issn=0031-9171}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hasegawa|first1=A.|last2=Mima|first2=K.|date=1978|title=Anomalous transport produced by kinetic Alfvén wave turbulence|journal=Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics|language=en|volume=83|issue=A3|pages=1117–1123|doi=10.1029/JA083iA03p01117|bibcode=1978JGR....83.1117H|issn=2156-2202}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Diamond|first1=P. H.|last2=Hasegawa|first2=A.|last3=Mima|first3=K.|date=2011|title=Vorticity dynamics, drift wave turbulence, and zonal flows: a look back and a look ahead|journal=Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion|volume=53|issue=12|article-number=124001|doi=10.1088/0741-3335/53/12/124001|bibcode=2011PPCF...53l4001D|s2cid=21051033 |issn=0741-3335|url=http://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/7885/fb802d7e333b517cbe7923b8316bc71638ac.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190226224945/http://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/7885/fb802d7e333b517cbe7923b8316bc71638ac.pdf|archive-date=2019-02-26}}</ref> and in particular the derivation of the [[Hasegawa–Mima equation]] in 1977,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hasegawa|first1=A.|last2=Mima|first2=K.|date=1977|title=Stationary Spectrum of Strong Turbulence in Magnetized Nonuniform Plasma|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=39|issue=4|pages=205–208|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.39.205|bibcode=1977PhRvL..39..205H}}</ref> which won him the 2011 [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Stroth|first1=U|last2=Hidalgo|first2=C|date=2011-11-14|title=38th European Physical Society Conference on Plasma Physics|journal=Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion|language=en|volume=53|issue=12|article-number=120201|doi=10.1088/0741-3335/53/12/120201|s2cid=250854312|issn=0741-3335|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Mima studied physics at [[Kyoto University]] and graduated with a [[bachelor's degree]] in 1968 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1973. He was a post-doctoral student at [[Hiroshima University]] until 1975 and then started work at [[Osaka University]], where he became an assistant professor in 1978 and a professor in 1984. From 1995 to 1999, he was director of the Institute of Laser Engineering. There, his work involved [[laser fusion]] (experiments with the [[GEKKO XII|Gekko XII laser]] and FIREX program), [[Free-electron laser|free electron lasers]], [[relativistic plasma]]s and laser-plasma interaction.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37322151400|title=K. Mima|website=[[IEEE]]|access-date=2020-03-14}}</ref>

Mima died on 5 January 2025, at the age of 79.<ref>[https://www.ile.osaka-u.ac.jp/ja/2025/01/08/post-13047/index.html 【訃報】大阪大学名誉教授 三間圀興先生] {{in lang|ja}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Mima was a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1988&unit_id=DPP&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-03-14}}</ref> and a Member of the [[Physical Society of Japan]] and the Japan Society of Plasma Science at Nuclear Fusion Research.<ref name=":0" />

He was a co-recipient of the 1993 [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/dawson.cfm|title=John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-03-14}}</ref> and won the 2007 [[Edward Teller Award]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ans.org/honors/recipients/va-teller|title=ANS / Honors and Awards / Recipients / Edward Teller Award|website=www.ans.org|access-date=2020-03-14}}</ref> He was jointly awarded the 2011 [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] (with [[Akira Hasegawa]] and [[Patrick H. Diamond]]) for ''"laying the foundations of modern numerical transport simulations and key contributions on self-generated [[Zonal flow (plasma)|zonal flows]] and flow shear decorrelation mechanisms which form the basis of modern [[turbulence]] in plasmas".''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://plasma.ciemat.es/eps/awards/alfven-prize/|title=Alfvén Prize {{!}} European Physical Society – Plasma Physics Division|language=en-US|access-date=2020-03-14}}</ref>
